newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN MONEY RATES CLOSE UP AS LIQUIDITY TIGHTENS.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN MONEY RATES CLOSE UP AS LIQUIDITY TIGHTENS.

text.p: Extremely tight liquidity in the banking system pushed Taiwan's money rates to higher close on Monday, despite the central bank's persistent fund injections, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate surged to as high as 10.5 percent before easing to 9.852 percent at close against Saturday's 9.525 finish -- doubling the the central bank's previously declared 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper rose to 8.75-9.00 percent from 8.50-8.75.
The central bank, responding to recent tight liquidity in the money market, continued to launch open market operations on Monday, injecting T$15 billion worth of funds into the banking system.

Despite the central bank's move, dealers said tax payments, state auction of 182 million in China Steel and central bank's bid to support the Taiwan dollar in the foreign exchange market all tightened liquidity.
The interbank rate is likely to move at between 10.00 and 10.50 range on Tuesday.
The bond market stayed in a narrow-range consolidation due to a lack of trading interest.
The benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was traded at 6.1375 percent against 6.1350.
